entities.name: Balista
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Balista, a high-ranking military officer, most likely the praetorian prefect under Emperor Valerian, emerged as a pivotal figure during the chaotic Crisis of the Third Century (235–284 CE). Following Valerian's catastrophic capture by Shapur I of the Sasanian Empire in 260 CE, Balista, alongside Macrianus Major, orchestrated the proclamation of Macrianus's sons, Macrianus Minor and Quietus, as emperors in the Roman East. His strategic acumen and control over the remaining Eastern legions made him instrumental in the initial success of this significant usurpation against the legitimate emperor Gallienus, temporarily fracturing Roman imperial authority.

Balista's operational base was primarily the Roman province of Syria, where he managed to consolidate control over substantial forces. He was responsible for securing the eastern frontier against the Sasanians and, crucially, for defending the usurpers' holdings against loyalist Roman forces and the rising power of Odaenathus of Palmyra. Notably, Balista successfully defended the strategically vital city of Emesa, demonstrating his tactical capabilities. While Macrianus Major and Macrianus Minor marched west to confront Gallienus, Balista remained in the East with Quietus, holding the line against a resurgent Roman central authority and regional contenders.

The Macrianic usurpation, heavily reliant on Balista's military and administrative talents, ultimately failed. After Macrianus Major and Minor were defeated and killed in Illyricum by Gallienus's general Aureolus in 261 CE, Quietus and Balista were left isolated in the East. Quietus was subsequently murdered in Emesa, likely by Odaenathus, who then turned his attention to Balista. Details of Balista's death are debated, with some accounts suggesting he was also killed by Odaenathus, possibly in Emesa or during a siege, marking the swift end of this significant challenge to Gallienus's rule.
